text: scriptorium — a co-present markdown editor: the human edits, you write new versions.
open [path...] [--no-open] [--restore ..] [--timeout ..] [--start-timeout ..]
spawn a session (opens the browser), adding paths; prints {url, port, session_id}. --timeout <seconds> sets the idle close (default 1800); --timeout 0 stands until closed
add <path...>                                 add files or folders to the context list
state [--full]                                the session: context, docs + versions (with paths), active, dirty, selection
tail [--since ..] [--once]                    the human's messages (with selection + active path) as JSON lines — wrap with Monitor; its last line names the next act
version-new [--doc ..] [--from ..] [--label ..]
copy a version (default: the active one) to a new file; prints its path to edit
say [text...] [--stdin] [--body-file ..]      post a chat message from the agent (prose: --body-file <path> or --stdin)
version-delete <vN> [--doc ..]                remove a version and its file (never the active one — activate another first)
task [text...] [--stdin] [--body-file ..]     say you have started something; prints the id to finish it with
task-status <id> <status...>                  say what step a task is on (for work worth watching)
task-done <id> [outcome...]                   mark a task finished, optionally saying what came of it
task-remove <id>                              forget a task entirely — for one started by mistake
tasks-clear                                   forget every finished task; outstanding ones are left alone
working [--for ..]                            say you are still on it — silences the waiting nudge, keeps the human's pulse
note [text...] [--doc ..] [--quote ..] [--stdin] [--body-file ..]
note a passage of the active version (--quote 'exact text'; prose: --body-file or --stdin)
notes [--doc ..] [--full]                     the notes on a document, placed in the active version (--full includes resolved)
note-edit <id> [text...] [--doc ..] [--stdin] [--body-file ..]
rewrite what a note says (its passage is unchanged)
note-resolve <id> [--doc ..] [--reopen]       mark a note dealt with (--reopen puts it back)
note-remove <id> [--doc ..]                   delete a note
diff <against> [--doc ..] [--context ..] [--patch]
compare the active version with another (vN or 'saved' for the file on disk); --patch for plain unified text
merge <against> [--doc ..] [--hunks ..]       take changes from another version into the active one (--hunks 1,3; default: all of them)
activate <vN> [--doc ..]                      make a version the active one (the one the human edits and Save writes)
new-doc <path>                                create an empty document (its folder must be a set, a folder in one, or the workspace)
new-folder <path>                             create a folder — inside a set, or in the workspace as a new set
move <path> <into>                            move a document or folder into another folder (a real move on disk)
rename <path> <name>                          rename a document or folder in place
hide <path>                                   remove a document, folder or set from Scriptorium — the files stay on disk
unhide <entry>                                bring back everything hidden in a set (its entry id, from state)
make-set <path>                               turn a single document into a set: a folder named for it, the document moved in
import <file> [--into ..]                     copy a document in (default: into the workspace) and show the copy
workspace [dir]                               print the workspace (where drops and new top-level documents land), or set it
meta [path]                                   a document's frontmatter as the daemon read it (no path: every context document)
find [--type ..] [--status ..] [--lifecycle ..] [--tag ..] [--since ..]
documents by frontmatter — filters AND, all optional; an empty result is an answer (count)
search <query...> [--limit ..]                search the context: fuzzy on names, exact in text — searches the ACTIVE version of open documents, which grep cannot see
doctor                                        what is worth looking at in this session — each finding names the verb that fixes it
forget [--doc ..]                             forget a document whose file of record is gone (refused while the file exists — use hide to take one out of the context)
dangling [--entry ..]                         links in a set that nothing answers — file, line, and the target as written
graph [--entry ..]                            a set's map as JSON — nodes, edges (body links and frontmatter kept apart), dangling
backlinks <path>                              what cites a document — `related` (frontmatter) and `links` (body), kept apart
meta-init <path> [--type ..] [--by ..]        add a frontmatter block to a document that has none (type guessed from its neighbours)
meta-set <path> <key=value...>                set frontmatter keys — one line edit each, everything else untouched
info                                          print the resolved session pointer
close                                         shut the session down (the manifest stays, for open --restore)
version                                       this CLI's {name, version} as JSON (alias: --version, -V)
schema                                        this CLI's machine-readable interface (acc declaration v0)
help                                          show this message (alias: --help, -h)
--help | -h | --version | -V  root tokens: help, or {name, version} as JSON
Add --session <id> to any verb that talks to a session (default: most recent).
Each verb accepts only the flags on its row.
Output: JSON on stdout, one document per answer — except tail (one JSON line
per event) and help (prose). Failures: one JSON envelope on stderr, exit
2 = usage, 1 = internal, 5 = not found, 6 = conflict. tail waits for a
session rather than failing, and ends 0 when its session closes. tail
ends itself before Monitor's 30-minute cap with a line naming the next act; a human watching a terminal keeps it open with SPELLBOOK_TAIL_WINDOW_MS=0.
